SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Seller's draft is the counterparty's position; nothing in it binds us or creates playbook authority. No Amelia Frost written approval exists for any fallback. All items below remain OPEN unless stated.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- Seller: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- Buyer wants: 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- Recommendation: **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m.** The 20% figure is only a conditional fallback requiring Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft, and none has been given.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- Seller: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery (cl 12.2).
- Buyer wants: de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; tipping (first-dollar) basket.
- Recommendation: **Reject on all three elements.** Seller's thresholds are 5x our positions and the excess-only structure would permanently forfeit the first AUD 250,000 of valid loss.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- Seller: 18 months (cl 12.3/13), plus a "all limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated" rule.
- Buyer wants: 24 months after Completion.
- Recommendation: **Reject; counter at 24 months and strike the default-application language.** 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given), and the catch-all rule is a hidden general-regime override.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- Seller: capacity and title warranties collapsed into general caps/time limits "for administrative simplicity."
- Buyer wants: separate regime – 100% of price cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- Recommendation: **Reject outright; this is non-negotiable.** Capping title at 20% with an 18-month window means we could pay AUD 24m for shares we don't own and recover at most AUD 4.8m.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- Seller: no fraud carve-out; limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5).
- Buyer wants: fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable.
- Recommendation: **Reject; insist on express carve-out in each of cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5 and Schedule-level limitations.** This is a mandatory position that no one on our side may waive.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- Seller: general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2; Sched 7).
- Buyer wants: specific, fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Recommendation: **Reject paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2; require a "fair disclosure with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope" standard against specific warranties.** Whole-data-room disclosure would effectively disclose against every warranty and gut the warranty package.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- Seller: no claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- Buyer wants: delete blanket exclusion; any qualifier limited to named seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry; never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- Recommendation: **Delete cl 8.3 in full.** "Discoverable" knowledge imputed to advisers is a constructive-knowledge bar that, combined with SPA-N-006, would eliminate almost all warranty recourse.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- Seller: reasonable endeavours only; condition deemed satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent (cl 3/6.3). Disclosure Letter ¶2 confirms no final consent and no evidence of cl 11.3 conditions being met.
- Buyer wants: effective consent AND evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied as a condition precedent to Completion.
- Recommendation: **Reject; redraft as a hard CP requiring unconditional effective consent plus documentary evidence of condition satisfaction.** Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m), and a consent that is "delivered" but conditional is not a consent.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- Seller: ~AUD 3.2m facility to be addressed by a post-Completion release (cl 2/7). Disclosure Letter ¶3 confirms not repaid, no discharge in data room.
- Buyer wants: current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion.
- Recommendation: **Reject; require payout letter, funds-flow repayment and executed releases/PPSR discharges delivered at Completion.** A post-Completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable bank undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval, neither of which exists; cash-free/debt-free cannot be achieved with secured debt still outstanding.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- Seller: DD-005 AUD 420,000 closing bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. Disclosure Letter ¶5 confirms exclusion and is silent on on-costs.
- Buyer wants: AUD 420,000 plus triggered payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or expressly seller-funded.
- Recommendation: **Reject; require a specific line item (bonuses + on-costs) deducted from price or paid by Seller via funds flow, with a backstop indemnity.** Silent exclusion means the Company (i.e. us post-Completion) bears the cost, which is a price leak of at least AUD 420,000 plus on-costs.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- Seller: indemnity confined to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). Disclosure Letter ¶4: DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 materials on full payment; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- Buyer wants: broadened indemnity covering loss from any defect in title to or transfer of Project Materials, with the SOW3 payment cure preserved.
- Recommendation: **Reject as too narrow; broaden to cover IP ownership/transfer failure and related loss, keep the cure route of paying SOW3 fees and obtaining confirmatory assignment pre-Completion.** The AUD 180,000 is unverified either way, so treat it as an open exposure to be cured or indemnified, not as a settled fact.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- Seller: "preliminary operational matter," not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sched 6). Disclosure Letter ¶6: ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address; access, scope and notification duty undetermined; no confirmed breach, no loss amount.
- Buyer wants: log preservation, completed investigation, regular updates, and a position consistent with no assumed conclusion in either direction.
- Recommendation: **Do not accept the "not material" characterisation; require a pre-Completion covenant to preserve logs, complete the investigation, provide updates, and a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident, while assuming no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand.** The matter cannot be waved through or priced until the investigation closes.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)**
- Seller: ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure Letter ¶8: three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (DD-008/DD-011); silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- Buyer wants: an assessment of timing, scope, terminability and accrual before any treatment is agreed.
- Recommendation: **Treat as open for DD assessment; do not concede ordinary-course status, but do not automatically classify as Debt or seek a price deduction.** Request the contracts and accrual position so the treatment can be decided on evidence.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- Seller: single regime for all Claims; limitations apply "to all Claims of any nature"; Title/Tax/IP folded into the general regime; cl 12.3 default-application rule.
- Buyer wants: Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations and covenants as distinct categories with their own caps, periods and exclusions, no hidden general-regime override.
- Recommendation: **Reject; insert an express "general limitations do not apply to…" carve-out listing Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenant breaches.** The Seller's structure would use administrative simplicity to subordinate every protected category to a 20% cap and 18-month window.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- Seller: title to 100% of shares evidenced by the company share register at DD-012. Disclosure Letter ¶10 acknowledges this is the source relied on, not Buyer verification.
- Buyer wants: independent ASIC searches, PPSR searches, board/shareholder authority evidence, encumbrance confirmations and share certificates.
- Recommendation: **Do not rely on DD-012; obtain independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence as a Completion deliverable and CP.** An internal register prepared by the Seller is a supplied source, not independent proof, and the Riverlark security may extend to the shares.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- Seller: tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime."
- Buyer wants: separate tax and IP regimes with their own caps, periods and basket treatment, to be negotiated.
- Recommendation: **Reject the characterisation as settled; mark both as OPEN.** Nothing has been agreed, and we assume neither unlimited liability nor resolution – these terms are to be negotiated independently of SPA-N-001 to 003.

---

## Summary

Across all 16 issues the Seller's package is below our starting position and in several cases (SPA-N-004, 005, 007, 014) would structurally defeat buyer protection. None of the Seller's figures match any authorised fallback, and no Amelia Frost written authority has been given for any deviation. Recommend a full mark-up reinstating playbook positions, with Bluefen, Riverlark, employee bonuses and title verification treated as Completion-critical.

Note: the Disclosure Letter's own ¶11 reservation confirms the Seller is not asserting any conclusion on these points, which supports our position that nothing is "settled."
